The Qua’an-Pan Local Government Council of Plateau State has imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew on Doemak District following heightened tension after suspected gunmen burnt down seven houses in Bong community. The curfew, which runs from 6pm to 6am daily, was imposed on Monday evening amid reports that residents were fleeing their homes, shops had closed and commercial activities had been disrupted over fears of further attacks. The Director of Press and Publicity to the Executive Chairman of the council, Danaan Sylvanus, announced the restriction in a public notice issued on Monday. He said, “In view of the security tension, Qua’an-Pan Local Government Council has imposed a curfew in Doemak. “The curfew shall be observed from 6pm to 6am. By this notice, any person found moving during this period will be treated as a security threat by the security agencies.” The council urged residents to comply strictly with the directive and cooperate with security agencies to maintain peace in the area. The curfew followed Sunday’s attack on Bong community in Doemak District, where suspected gunmen reportedly stormed the village around 9pm and set seven houses ablaze. A community source, Silas Bishop, who confirmed the attack, lamented the destruction and called on security operatives to intensify efforts to track down and arrest those responsible. Meanwhile, tension has reportedly gripped Doemak, the headquarters of Qua’an-Pan Local Government Area, with residents said to be packing their belongings and relocating to safer places over fears for their lives and property. As of Monday evening, shops were reportedly shut, while commercial activities had been disrupted as residents expressed concern over the security situation. Confirming the attack, the Executive Chairman of Qua’an-Pan Local Government Council, Christopher Audu Manship, condemned the incident and assured residents that the government would not abandon them. He said, “Government will not abandon the people of Bong community. We will support efforts towards the restoration of the houses destroyed and sustain measures to secure the community against further attacks.” The chairman urged youths in the affected communities to remain vigilant and promptly report suspicious movements to security agencies. The attack on Bong community occurred around the same time suspected terrorists invaded Zwagal community in Jipal District of neighbouring Mangu Local Government Area, where several residents were killed. Manship, who visited Zwagal alongside the Executive Chairman of Mangu Local Government Council, Emmanuel Bala Mwolpun, described the attack as barbaric and inhuman. He said, “The government will intensify efforts to secure lives and property, which remains the primary responsibility of every government.” The Qua’an-Pan chairman also conveyed Governor Caleb Mutfwang’s condolences to the bereaved families in Zwagal, saying the governor remained determined to tackle insecurity in the state. Also speaking, Mwolpun assured residents that efforts were being made to improve network services in the affected communities to enhance security surveillance and communication. Earlier, the Long Zwagal, Miskagam Jonathan Wadong, thanked the two council chairmen for their prompt response and mobilisation of security personnel following the attack. He said gunshots suddenly rang out in the community at about 8pm before the attackers invaded, throwing residents into panic. Wadong appealed to the government to deploy more security personnel to the area to prevent a recurrence of the attacks. James Abraham
